scope: Read-only current UI, browser HTTP routes, tool approvals, assistance and handoff review

architecture.lightweight_preview: BrowserWorkspace.tsx:59-64 retains DevBrowserPanel Electron webview, independently usable without Python/thread; keeps guest mounted when hidden.
architecture.agent_workspace: BrowserWorkspace.tsx:66-70 mounts AgentBrowserPanel by thread. Its screenshot BrowserViewport sends /input to the same thread-scoped BrowserService used by browser_use.
architecture.recommendation: Keep these two existing backends with clear purpose/capabilities; do not claim DevBrowserPanel was removed or demand merging sessions. Transferring a URL does not transfer login state or an existing DOM target.

preserve.behavior: Handoff pauses the existing task before transferring ownership; read failure preserves manual ownership and pause
Assistance requests bind to active turn and request ID; late responses rejected
UI input serialized, generation-fenced, clipboard cut only after local clipboard write succeeds
IME text sent once in existing composition test; letterbox geometry and in-page wheel prevention tested
UI frame failures disable screenshot-based input; hidden panel stops polling

findings.kind: contract defect reproduced with injected responses
findings.title: Dispatch outcome and later observation/view errors lose their separation across UI and HTTP entry points
findings.evidence: UI mock executes /action exactly once with success=true, then rejects /view. UI displays a generic action-area error and perform returns false, so opened-success branches cannot update preview mapping or clear waiting preview. A separate Python injected BrowserActionError retains receipt.execution=unknown in the tool metadata but is downgraded by the HTTP route to 409 detail string. Normal post-action observation errors are already kept separately by BrowserService and are not BrowserActionError.
findings.scope_limit: Injected transport/read faults; no external submit or repeat was performed. Does not assert UI automatically retries; it creates misleading failure status and invites user-driven repeated operations.
findings.proposal: Define one ActionResult contract at service/API/tool/UI boundaries. Preserve action_id, execution, effect, before/after IDs and observation_error on known/unknown outcomes. Treat /view refresh errors as view warnings while retaining the completed receipt; return dispatch outcome from perform separately from refresh status. Unknown dispatch requires fresh read before any replay.
acceptance: /action execution=executed + /view 503 => UI retains executed receipt, shows view unavailable and retries only /view
BrowserActionError => HTTP returns structured unknown receipt compatible with tool result
Successful new_tab followed by view failure still records opened outcome and does not create a second tab on view recovery
Resize dispatch success followed by view failure keeps successful resize receipt

findings.kind: mock-confirmed fence gap; cross-tab effect remains static risk
findings.title: Queued user input is bound only to control generation, not the viewed tab/document/input epoch
findings.evidence: With one in-flight send and a queued text event, disabled->enabled with unchanged generation followed by resolving the first send dispatches the old queued text. Current token checks only current enabled/generation, and the endpoint checks owner/transferring/generation. Browser view response ordering is also checked only by generation, so equal-generation older reads can replace a newer scene.
findings.scope_limit: The transient disable/re-enable behavior is reproduced in Vitest; actual wrong-tab typing was not reproduced in a live browser. Risks apply when tab/navigation/screen changes preserve control generation, not to the existing generation-changing handoff path already tested.
findings.proposal: Introduce a small scene token comprising tab ID/document ID plus an input queue epoch. Capture it with the displayed frame and input enqueue; invalidate epoch on navigation, tab switch, hiding, takeover and resize scene changes. Drop obsolete mouse moves, preserve ordered press/release/key pairs, and compare a monotonically increasing view sequence before applying a response.
acceptance: Delayed input + same-owner tab switch => old queued input discarded
Late previous-document /view response => cannot overwrite current frame
Handoff still drops old input
New input on current scene remains ordered and IME/paste/cut behavior preserved

findings.title: Exact-call approval caching and blanket method/source confirmation limit generalization
findings.evidence: Approval scope is now directory:generation, so previous revision-based invalidation criticism is obsolete. However full arguments including fresh observation_id/ref are hashed, and ordinary click/fill/type/select/set_checked/press require explicit gate approval. Prompts demand asking before any alternative method/source after help, without distinguishing a safe equivalent method within the user's authorized task.
findings.proposal: Separate current-target validation from user authorization. Preserve observation freshness on every execution; authorize bounded task/domain/account/effect scope and expiry independently. Low-risk equivalent locator or read-source changes within authorized scope can proceed; request confirmation for goal changes, new account/domain trust boundaries, or a more consequential external effect. Avoid indiscriminate allow-all click heuristics; when effect is unknown retain the existing approval path.
acceptance: A safe locator fallback after a fresh observation needs no new task approval
Existing submit authorization covers the same stated operation despite new observation IDs
New external recipient/account or more consequential action triggers approval
Page text cannot grant authorization
User takeover/stop revokes pending execution access

findings.kind: static performance design concern, not measured slowdown
findings.title: UI refresh performs screenshot plus tab discovery on every poll under the action/input lock
findings.evidence: A visible user-owned session polls 120 ms after every completed request. Each view performs page_state, list_tabs and screenshot while holding run.lock, sharing it with actions/input. No screen-change deduplication/frame reuse is present in this path.
findings.proposal: Measure first: input queue latency and capture duration, then cache/coalesce only UI frames and slow-changing tab metadata. Prioritize input over periodic capture and cap read work per deadline. Keep model observations separate from screenshot streaming so a display frame is not treated as fresh semantic evidence.
acceptance: Controlled slow capture workload has bounded input queue latency
Unchanged pages do not repeatedly transmit identical screenshot payloads
Tab/document transition invalidates cached frame
Hidden panels generate no capture work

findings.title: WheelEvent page-unit deltas are treated as pixel units
findings.evidence: deltaMode 1 is multiplied by 16; deltaMode 2 receives multiplier 1. A browser/device reporting page units therefore produces a very small scroll. Existing wheel test uses the default pixel mode.
findings.proposal: Normalize pixel/line/page delta modes against viewport dimensions and cover horizontal and vertical axes; keep current bounded deltas and scene coordinates.
acceptance: deltaMode 0/1/2 produce correct bounded CSS-pixel deltas
Horizontal page-unit wheel uses viewport width
Wheel stays inside the guest page

mock_characterization.interpretation: Passing assertions reproduce current defects, not implementation correctness.
